question.prompt: Cassandra sets her watch to the correct time at noon. At the actual time of \(1{:}00\) PM, she notices that her watch reads \(12{:}57\) and \(36\) seconds. Assuming that her watch loses time at a constant rate, what will be the actual time when her watch first reads \(10{:}00\) PM?

solutions.explanation:
Measure both elapsed times from noon, when the watch was correct. In \(60\) actual minutes, the watch advances
\[
57+\frac{36}{60}=57.6\text{ minutes}.
\]
Because its rate is constant, the ratio of displayed elapsed time to actual elapsed time is always
\[
\frac{57.6}{60}=\frac{24}{25}.
\]
From noon to a displayed \(10{:}00\) PM is \(10\) hours, or \(600\) displayed minutes. If \(t\) is the actual number of minutes since noon, then
\[
\frac{24}{25}t=600,
\qquad
 t=600\cdot\frac{25}{24}=625.
\]
This is \(10\) hours and \(25\) minutes after noon. The watch advances steadily at a positive rate, so this is the first time it reaches that reading. The actual time is \(10{:}25\) PM, choice C.
solutions.title: Compare watch time with actual time
